The petition was filed before the LAC and referred to by the Collector for determination of the court.

2. The brief factual matrix leading to the present petition is that the Government vide notification bearing No. F.11(19)/2001/L&B/LA/20112 dt. 21.03.2003 issued by the Lt. Governor of Delhi under Section 4 of the Act, Government intended to acquire about 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas of land with its Kamal Sharma (1605-06) vs Union Of India (Mubarakpur Dabas) on 14 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88977039/

sentences.text: The Government vide consequent Declaration/notification No. F.11 (19)/2001/L&B/LA/28176 dated 19.03.2004 issued pursuant thereto under Section 6 of the Act, acquired 2480 Bigha 01 Biswas land (as detailed in the statement under Section 19 of the Act), situated in the revenue estate of village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi.
The LAC (N/W)

after completing all the requisite formalities as provided under the Act, announced the Award bearing no. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 u/s 11 of the Act in respect of 2480 bighas 01 biswas out of the aforesaid said land and awarded a compensation at the uniform rate of Rs.15,70,000/ per acre (or Rs. 3,27,083.33/ per bigha) for the entire said land in addition to other statutory benefits and interests.

4. It is stated that the petitioners are the recorded owner/bhumidhar of the land comprised in Khasra no. 16//18 (100), having share as per the revenue record, situated in the revenue estate of Village Mubarakpur Dabas, Delhi (in short, the said land).
5.

It is stated that the Award passed by the ld. LAC is not acceptable to the petitioners and,
therefore, this reference has been filed with a view to reassess the market value of the land which has been wrongly assessed by the LAC.
6.

It is submitted by the petitioner that the compensation amount awarded by LAC is too low,
inadequate, arbitrary, unjust, illusory, etc and LAC no. 09/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW))
Kamal Sharma Vs. Union of India Page no. 3 of 10 without any reasonable basis.

sentences.text: The land in questions is free from all encumbrances i.e. family disputes, court cases, sales, mortgage, Legal Notice, third party interest, gift, etc and is fully fertile, completely leveled and ideally situated and yields three crops in the year regularly.

All types of irrigation facilities like, electric connection,
tubewell, canal with sweet water are available in the said land.
The land in question is situated on the main Mundka Karala road and near Village Abadi.

7. The land in question is adjoining the industrial area and all facilities like transportation, hospitals,
renowned schools, Post office, police station, telephone, drinking water, office of the North Delhi Power Ltd, etc are available in the revenue estate of vill. Mubarakpur Dabas.
The said area is surrounded by developed colonies, farmhouses, etc namely Meer Vihar, Sharma Enclave, Dhruv Enclave, Agar Nagar, etc.
The largest colony in Asia Rohini and Rohini Ext. and Nangloi Ext, Swaran Park, Rajdhani Park is only 2 KM from the revenue estate of land in question.
The railway station of Northen Railway Mundka is only 2 KM from the land in question.
8. The Ld. LAC has not considered the facts while announcing the award the value of the land in vill.

Mubarakpur Dabas itself is more than Rs. 15,000/ per sq. Yards in Karala more than Rs. 30,000/
in Nangloi, Ghewra Industrial area, Mundka Industrial Areas more than Rs. 30,000/ per sq. Yards and also nearby colonies.

sentences.text: The LAC has not legally assessed the market value of the land rather he has wholly and solely relied on the policy announcement and which come into effect from the financial year 20012002 in which the Government fixed the indicative prices of agricultural land at the rate of Rs. 15.70 lacs per acre for the acquisition of the Agricultural land.
The LAC has further not made any efforts to find out the market value of the land in the village.

10. It is stated that in view of these facts and circumstances and keeping in view the consideration of the petitioners, petitioners are claiming compensation for their acquired land at Rs. 30,000/ per sq. yards.
The petitioners have claimed a solatium @ 30% on the market value and additional amount.
Interest at the rate of 18% p.a. from the date of realization of the amount.
A sum of Rs. 5 lakhs to the petitioner on account of change of profession and losses in profession.
Alternative plot to the petitioner be awarded alongwith a cost of Rs. 10,000/ per tress alongwith any other relief as per law.

11. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.1 /UOI and, it is, inter alia,
submitted the reference petition is not maintainable as the same is barred by time.
It is further submitted that the Ld. LAC has correctly assessed the market value of the land in question prevailing at the time of issuance of notification under section4 of LA Act.

All the other LAC no.
09/ 2016 (Award No. 16/200506/DC(NW)) Kamal Sharma Vs. Union of India Page no. 5 of 10 averments made by the petitioner have been denied fully.

sentences.text: It is therefore submitted that the present petition is based on false, frivolous grounds and as such merits dismissal.

12. Written statement has been filed on behalf of respondent no.2/DDA and, inter alia, it is submitted that the ld. LAC while passing the impugned Award in respect of village Mubarakpur Dabas had taken into consideration the market value of the land on the basis of the sale deeds of the adjoining lands of the area as well as the other documents which were made available to ld. LAC.
The area of the land and other amenities/facilities were also taken into consideration while assessing the compensation.

13. It is submitted that the compensation awarded by ld. LAC is adequate, sufficient just and legal and is based on cogent and reliable evidence, therefore, there is no scope for enhancement of the compensation amount.
The present reference petition is also barred by limitation.

The copy of the reference petition has not been forwarded to DDA, though the DDA is a beneficiary party, therefore,
DDA is not liable to pay any interest on the delayed period.

It is submitted that as per the directions of Land and Building Department, after announcement of the Award reference should be forwarded by LAC within 60 days from the date of filing of the reference.
The present petition has not been forwarded to the court within 60 days therefore, DDA/beneficiary of land is not liable to pay interest thereupon.

sentences.text: I have heard the Ld. Counsels for the parties and have perused the entire record including the documents and the evidence led by the parties.
I have given a thoughtful consideration to the same.

My issue wise findings and determination are as under : 
1.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for enhancement in compensation, if yes, then to what extent?
OPP 18.

19. To prove its case, the petitioner, through his counsel have adopted the evidence led in case Savitri Devi (supra).
During the course of arguments, he has relied upon the judgment passed in the aforementioned case on 05.09.2023 and Ld.
Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the petitioners may also be awarded compensation as awarded to the petitioners in the aforementioned case.
20. Even, the respondents have also relied upon the evidence led by the respondents in the aforementioned case and no separate evidence has been led by them in the present case.

sentences.text: In view of the aforesaid discussion, this court also determines the same enhanced market value in the present case, in so far as the acquisition of the land of petitioners is concerned.

22. In the case of Savitri Devi (supra), this court had adjudicated the market value of land of village Mubarkpur Dabas acquired through Award No. 16 of 200506 dated 14.09.2005 as Rs. 19,45,800/
per acre i.e. an enhancement of Rs. 3,75,800/ per acre has been given.
There is no evidence on record to gather that the land of the petitioners herein was in any way inferior to the land involved in Savitri Devi (supra).
The petitioners are, accordingly entitled to the same compensation for their land as was awarded in Savitri Devi (supra).
This court adjudicate the market value of land of the petitioners as Rs.19,45,800/ per acre thereby giving an enhancement of Rs.3,75,800/ per acre.
23. The petitioners have not led any evidence with respect to alleged damages of the growing crops and structures or other claims.
Therefore, the petitioners shall not be entitled to any damages on the aforesaid counts.
This issue is decided accordingly in favour of the petitioners.
